topics.name: equate

topics.summary: Return the top event's boolean equation as R builds it: repeatedly replace each gate name (first occurrence per set, gates in row order) with that gate's set until no gate name remains; the first row's set is the answer.
topics.description: Return the top event's boolean equation as R builds it: repeatedly replace each gate name (first occurrence per set, gates in row order) with that gate's set until no gate name remains; the first row's set is the answer. * is AND, + is OR, and every gate keeps its " (...) " wrapping, e.g. " ( ( (B * (C + D) ) * (A + (B * C) ) ) ) " for fakenodes/fakeedges.

topics.name: concentrate
topics.title: concentrate
topics.summary: Minimal cut sets of the tree in data (the output of curate()).
topics.description:
Minimal cut sets of the tree in data (the output of curate()).

Returns a list of strings, one per minimal cut set, events joined by * in R's sorted order, sets ordered as admisc::simplify() orders them: fewer events first, then by the events' positions in the sorted event list. top is passed to mocus(): "or" (default) follows the equation, "and" reproduces R's current output (README, "Deviations from R").

topics.name: tabulate
topics.title: tabulate
topics.summary: data: minimal cutsets as strings (e.g. ["B*C", "A*B*D"], what concentrate() returns); formula: the formulate() function.
topics.description: data: minimal cutsets as strings (e.g. ["B*C", "A*B*D"], what concentrate() returns); formula: the formulate() function. Returns one row per cutset (sorted) with mincut, [query,] cutsets, failures, coverage, where cutsets counts failing truth-table rows that contain the cutset, failures counts all failing rows and coverage = cutsets / failures.

topics.name: mocus
topics.title: mocus
topics.summary: Every cut set of the tree in data (the output of curate()).
topics.description:
Every cut set of the tree in data (the output of curate()).

Returns a list of lists of basic-event names, one list per cut set (not yet minimal; concentrate() minimises). method takes R's labels; all three run the same pure-Python queue algorithm, which reproduces mocus_rcpp() and mocus_r() element for element ("mocus_original", R's historical loop, is accepted as a label only). top="or" (default) expands the top event as OR, as equate() does; top="and" expands it as AND, exactly as R's mocus() does today.

topics.name: validate_tree
topics.title: validate_tree
topics.summary: Check that nodes/edges describe a well-formed fault tree.
topics.description:
Check that nodes/edges describe a well-formed fault tree.

Fails closed: raises ValueError listing every problem found, returns True otherwise. Checks: required columns and node types; unique node ids; exactly one top node; every edge endpoint is a known id; every gate (top/and/or) has at least one child; basic events (not) have no children; and the graph has no cycle. A basic event shared by two branches is modelled as in R: the same event name on two distinct ids.
